utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, I understand there are some matters you wish to raise before the witness comes in.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Excuse me. So it's a problem about the intercepts. So it's about these intercepts, and that was the problem. Defence wishes to contest a number of these intercepts for various reasons; that was the problem. So after the hearing, with my learned friend, we tried to clear up the problem. There are other context-based evidence, and here I contest nothing of course, contextual evidence that I don't contest their use. It's not the nature of that evidence that worries me but it's the authenticity. The real problem is authenticity of the intercepts, at least of the ones mentioned and offered as contextual evidence by my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, two matters. Ordinarily, the witness would not have to be absent to discuss and determine these matters; and secondly, I understand that some of the intercepts you accept, others you contest their authenticity. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely. I haven't said anything about the witness, however. I didn't talk about the witness, about the fact that he should be there or should not be there. I didn't mention anything regarding that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really apologise about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we'll just continue in the absence of the witness, but could you inform the Chamber as to the basis on which you contest the authenticity of the intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, we didn't have a lot of time, but we already have some evidence that would be used and that go -- that prove that this person - and I'm talking about a specific person. Of course I will not mention that name because it's a Prosecution witness; it was planned as a Prosecution witness and you did not allow for him to be -- to sit here. And I won't mention his name for that reason. He was planned that he would testify with a pseudonym and he might, who knows, be called as a witness. But we have evidence that -- serious evidence that seem to prove that this intercept where this person is actually talking is not authentic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting, you wanted to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour. I -- just two points. The first is in -- from our point of view, this represents a change in the Defence's position with respect to intercepts because, of course, in the pre-trial conference, it's at page 222 to 223, the Defence indicated that they were accepting the authenticity of all the intercepts. Now, to be fair, I did then say, Before we finally decide on this and before we drop our intercept witnesses, let's be sure that we're talking about the same intercepts. I have then -- since then compiled a list of all the intercepts in our case, provided them to the Defence. I did that this morning. But all of the intercepts that are on our list were disclosed to the Defence a long time ago, most of them last year, only one of them this year, but all of them before the pre-trial conference when the Defence said we accept the authenticity of all the intercepts. But I suppose -- I suppose it's within the Defence's right to change their right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: They must put up their best defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's fine. That of course changes our position with respect to having to call those witnesses. I would suggest that since we have now provided a list of all the intercepts in the case that the Defence indicate to us -- respond to us and to indicate which ones they're challenging and then we can address those in whatever way is appropriate, whether we bring the intercept witness or it may require bringing the participant to the conversation here to testify, but I would suggest proceeding in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But as we're dealing with these specific intercepts, it would seem to the Chamber to be better to hear from the Defence which of these intercepts they accept and which they don't accept and the specific reasons for not doing so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that completely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And so this is what I want the Defence to do, to concentrate on the intercepts that are being put in by the Prosecution now and tell us which of them you accept and which of them you do not accept and the basis for your objection. Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, Mr. Robinson, I know very well, and that's what I learned in this Tribunal, what spoken word means and that the words spoken in front of you cannot be changed so easily and that no one should acknowledge and accept that. However, you remember very well on the first day - and that was the 10th of January - in response to Judge Robinson's question, I did say something about it and I'm not going to repeat it now. And at the end you concluded the hearing by leaving to both the Prosecution and the Defence to discuss this and primarily to establish whether both parties are referring and having the same thing in their minds. This, Mr. Robinson, happened in the first seven or eight minutes of that hearing. The first thing to do was for us to clearly understand whether we referred to the same thing, and that remained unclarified. Today Mr. Whiting invited us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tapuskovic. I must say that for myself, nothing that has happened here in my view affects the integrity of the Defence, not in any way whatsoever. Let us follow the procedure that I have outlined. So let us not waste any more time on this. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, just to respond to your question and I'm not disputing the conversation, the intercepts you're going to hear from my colleague, which specific intercepts are going to be addressed or dealt with today in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you may, by your leave --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I will tell you the numbers of the intercepts. We were offered as contextual evidence, so not contesting the nature of this of course, not contesting the use of this kind of evidence here, but this is what I have noted on the list that was addressed to me by the Prosecution. From the start, we accept the number 65 ter 24130. We accept that. It's not an intercept. I'm sorry, it's 24130 -- I'm just going to spell it out, 2430 --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That was marked as P37 yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: P37. Thank you, Ms. Edgerton. My colleague says it's P38. Which is it, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I stand corrected. Apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then the next exhibit is another 65 ter, 595.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And that was --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an intercept, and we are not contesting this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What was the exhibit number for that?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then the next exhibit, 2462, and it's another 65 ter exhibit. Here --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: With respect to 2462, I didn't offer that through the witness yesterday as any document nor as a contextual document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's not one of the documents --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have it on my list that I received from the Prosecution. It's on my list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, it would seem that it is not a document on which they're relying at this stage at any rate, so you need not concern yourself with that for the purposes of this exercise.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then that's all because the last exhibit that I wanted to mention is 2493 --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: P42 from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: In light of ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So let us be clear now. The intercepts that you accept are those that were marked for identification: P38, P39, and P42.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: But P38 was not an intercept, Your Honours, it was contextual document not an intercept. But again, those are the notes I have. I've been corrected already once early this afternoon and rightly so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Can I just ask --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: P38 is the document that appears to me to be an intercept between the accused and Ratko Mladic. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that's P39.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, for once our records here coincide with those of my friend. We have that marked as P39.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And the document we have marked as P38 bore the PT number 2430 which was not an intercept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So the documents that you do not accept are P38, P39, and P42, or rather, the documents that you accept are P38, P39, and P42?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: With my learned friend's confirmation, could I then ask that they be marked -- admitted as exhibits then, Your Honour. They were yesterday marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, they'll be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the following exhibits will be admitted: 65 ter 02430 marked for identification as P38 will be admitted as Exhibit P38. P595 marked for identification as P39 will be admitted as Exhibit P39. And 65 ter number 02493 was marked for identification as P42 and will be admitted as Exhibit P42.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now let us deal individually with those that you do not accept and hear the -- the basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as I have already said, these are intercepts in which a person was involved. I don't wish to pronounce this person's name in open session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If you wish --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a number of indications concerning this person and I don't wish to give his name in open session. This might make things easier because once the name is out, everybody will know exactly what intercept we are talking about. These four conversations are the conversation in which this particular person was involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let us go into private session and deal with them individually, not globally.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first intercept which also comes with a transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are we in private session?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So as you've already -- you've already talked to the Prosecution and now I'm going to cross-examine you on some items that are in your statement, a statement which is evidence here in this room. I'm going to ask you a few questions, of course which all have to do with that statement. Of course this statement dates back a few years. So first question: In your resume I don't think much has changed since you wrote this statement, but if I understood you right, when you arrived in Sarajevo, you already had been a military man for 19 years. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So if I'm right, you arrived in Sarajevo in May 1995 and stayed there until June 1996. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until May 1996 -- from May 1995 to May 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Then after that you stayed within IFOR?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, very briefly, I'd like to go through what's already been said, and I would like my assistant, Ms. Jovanovic, to help me and to have P27 on the screen if possible, that's Mr. Fortin's declaration -- statement. So if we could have that on the screen, please, at paragraph 14 until 14E. I'm sure we don't need to stay on this long because we'll agree this is the competence of the Sarajevo Sector, what the sector was responsible for. I have your statement here in English. Maybe I'll read it out in English, even though my English is not excellent. So these are total exclusion zones; right? In French it's "zone d'exclusion totale." If we could please have the paragraph 14A on the screen. [In English] "Maintaining observation post around the safe areas Sarajevo, Zepa, and Gorazde, see escorting humanitarian aid convoys to Zepa and Gorazde; D, guarding WCPs." [Interpretation] These WCPs were places where heavy weapons were collected. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So these were all the responsibilities that your sector was in charge of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So regarding the responsibilities of the sector, you also of course had your own job to do, and in that statement, in that same document, you talk about that. We need to check paragraphs 7 to 12 regarding that topic. So regarding this, from 7 to 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could please have those on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You say: [In English] "I was the operational staff. This included containing the sector commander everywhere. Meetings, briefings, media, interviews. I took notes of all those encounters and offered my perceptions, ideas, and advice on the situations they presented to the commander." [Interpretation] Is that accurate, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I still understand that you were with General Gobilliard, you were always with him, he was your boss.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Almost everywhere and almost all the time but sometimes of course I wasn't with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So in this job, you were really working on the ground, you were really mainly on Sarajevo and around Sarajevo. That is where you used to work.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 48 of the same document you state, and I quote. This is page 10. [In English] "I arrived in Sarajevo during the course of the second or third day of the Bosnian offensive to try and break out of the city." [Interpretation] So you arrived in Sarajevo during the course of the second or third day. You're not too sure whether it's the second or the third, but it was the second or the third day of the offensive of the Bosnian army, right, that's it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I was told. I was told that the offensive had just started.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you -- when you arrived, did you immediately understand that it was fierce combat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. A lot of Serbian shells were falling on the elevation around Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Then I guess that when you were moving around with your boss, General Gobilliard, you got accustomed to Sarajevo and the surroundings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mainly with the observation posts and the places where UN forces were stationed at first, at first anyway, and then I got to know the rest of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So if I've understood you right, they were on the territory held by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and also on the places that were held by the units of Republika Srpska, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the observation posts were mainly on the confrontation line between the two sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, on -- in your statement that we have just mentioned, you are mentioning a lot of names, geographical names, Debelo Brdo, for example, Nedzarici, Ilidza, it's correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please, I would like to talk about those names.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we please have the map on the ELMO, the map that we have in our -- in the bundle that was provided by the Prosecution. Could we please have one of those maps on the ELMO. I think it's the second one. The map is now on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This is a map that was developed by UNPROFOR, is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This is a map that has been provided for by our learned colleagues from Prosecution, and it's very handy to -- to use because there's this yellow line. Could you tell us exactly what this yellow line stands for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The yellow line represents the Bosnian front, and the red line the Serbian front.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, I'm sorry, it's not number 2. I'm being told it's number 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm sorry. I don't know exactly. I don't have my copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, proceed, because we have it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So we will look at a few place names that you mentioned in your statement. Grbavica, for example, could you show us on the map where it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's the urban zone that's south of Sarajevo right here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: What about Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: When we look at those two places that are surrounded on three sides, there are Serbian lines and Bosnian lines. Is it sort of a pocket? Do you think that we could talk about pockets here and say that Nedzarici and Grbavica were pockets? I mean militarily? When you look at this as a military man and you see this territory that is encircled on three sides.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, a pocket is -- an enclave is normally a place that you cannot get out of. Here it's more like a breakthrough. That would be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us exactly what is the military characteristic of this breakthrough?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Contrary to the enclave or the pockets which you cannot get out of, the breakthrough is where you move forward, where you can --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Compared to the enclave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because there's a way out.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But militarily, is it easy to hold this kind of position? I mean for the army as well as for the civilians that are inside because I'm sure you could confirm that these are urban areas with many densely populated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They're hard to hold. I'm sure that they're very hard to hold militarily.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: On this map, we also see other places that you mention and others that you don't mention, but I'm sure that you know of. Debelo Brdo, you mentioned it in your statement. Could you please point to it first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So could you confirm that this is -- that this is a mountain that's 799 metres high. Could you confirm that this is actually a mountain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is a mountain. We had an observation point up there, but I don't know exactly how high it is. I don't remember how high it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is it right behind the yellow line in a territory that would be held by the Bosnian -- the BH army, the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the observation points -- posts that we had were between the two lines. Now regarding this Debelo Brdo place that you are mentioning, I don't know exactly where it stood.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe you remember which unit held this Debelo Brdo place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the Bosnian or Serb? Is that what you're asking?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you're not sure so we can skip that. Do you know of another elevation that would be close to Debelo Brdo but more on the right, so to the north-east here on this map that would be called Colina Kapa?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may take us just back - apologies for the interruption - but just back to page 21, lines 15 and 16. I think that the witness asked the -- my learned friend to clarify whether she meant Bosnian or Serb. He didn't say he wasn't sure. But then my learned friend said at line 17, well, you're not sure so we can skip out. Perhaps we could just ask her to clarify her first question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you hear that, Ms. Isailovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'll do that right away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ask the witness the question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel, please, I thought I understood what you said, but could you please answer my question again. Are you -- or do you know exactly what unit held that elevation called Debelo Brdo, where there was an observation post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't say exactly. I don't know. I don't know exactly that place because this Debelo Brdo on the map is, you know, on -- it spreads on both sides of the line, so I can't say whether the site that you specifically talked about was held by Serbs or Bosnians. I can't say. All I can say is there was a French observation point and a Russian observation point on that elevation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, thank you. I understood the same thing before, but now I think everything is clear. There was another elevation Colina Kapa that I was telling you about. It's to the north-east of Debelo Brdo. This is an elevation that's 966 metres high. Do you remember it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: What about Zuc? It's here --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can move the map slightly on the -- towards the other side we could see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: On the screen it's on -- in the top, it's called Zuc. Do you see exactly where it is in the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: That's exactly it. This is an elevation 830 metres high. Do you remember that elevation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that elevation. I remember we had an observation point there, but I don't really remember how high it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So you see that it is in -- within the yellow line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So this elevation was controlled by the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So there's another elevation that is not mentioned on this map, but when you get close to Sarajevo it's just -- springs out. That's where the television antenna is located. It's called Mount Hum, H-u-m. Do you remember that mountain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I sort of remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So as you get close to Sarajevo, you see it right away with this television antenna on top.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I flew in, unfortunately; I didn't drive in.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can help you maybe. It's to the right of Mount Zuc and it's 816 metres high. Maybe you remember Mojmilo better because it's on the map and that would be at the very bottom of our map in the middle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So do you remember this elevation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we also had an observation here and we were watching especially the airport from this observation point.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So you confirm that this was close to the airport, and between -- and Dobrinja was between the airport and that mountain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And that is close to Nedzarici. And Dobrinja was controlled by Bosnian army, the Bosnian army, including Mojmilo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have lost the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the usher could just change the map and turn the page in the booklet, please, I'd like to see another map. Could you just scroll upwards a little bit, please. I would like to visualise Mount Igman which is on the left-hand side --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Map number 7? I'm not quite certain, Your Honours. Perhaps my friend could clarify for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From what the usher has just told me, this is map number 3. We have it now on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel, we can now resume. This is another map where we can see the scale. It's on a slightly larger scale. On the left-hand side we can see Mount Igman. Do you agree with me that this mountaintop dominates the city?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the western side of the town, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let him identify Mount Igman.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's this area here and to the west of the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that Mount Igman is the highest mount, with the exception of Bjelasnica, but Bjelasnica is a little bit further away, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can confirm. I don't know if it's the highest, but undoubtedly to the west of the valley where the airport is located and where the river comes down here, this was a very high mount, mountain, dominating the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you perhaps help us to identify something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we scroll the map upwards, please, a little.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And if you could identify at the foot of Mount Igman part of this city of Sarajevo which is called Hrasnica. Does this place name ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember the name. And I'm not quite sure where the area was located.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show us on this map where Ilidza is and where it is located.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Does Lukavica ring a bell because I -- I understand you've had to deal with this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It was a -- these were military barracks occupied by the Serbs, and the liaison officer of the SRK who we were dealing with was based here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you remember this: When you moved about, did you ever go to Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did go several times, but I navigated with a more detailed map and this was 12 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you could see Mount Igman from Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just below the airport, can you confirm that there was a tunnel at the time you arrived in Sarajevo? Can you confirm this for me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had heard -- we did hear about the tunnel for a while on the eastern side of the city, but I actually never used this outlet, this tunnel. I never went through it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But you did hear about this tunnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: At the time and today, do you remember what purpose this tunnel served? What was it used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now we shall move on to another topic because we haven't -- I haven't elicited much information from you on these maps. I just wanted to describe the area where you were from May 1995 until May 1996; in other words, where you were staying for one year. In your statement, you mention some --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Jovanovic, could we have a look at the statement. This is Exhibit number P27, paragraph 40, on page 8 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us tell us who this man was. This was a figure head. His name was misspelled in your statement. This is always a problem with Slavic names. This gentleman is mentioned in paragraph 40. His name is Aznadzic. It's Ajnadzic in fact, A-j-n-a-d-z-i-c. Do you remember this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As it is mentioned here, he was the commander of the 1st Bosnian Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. Of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of the 1st Corps of the Bosnian Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you get any detailed information about this corps of the Bosnian Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This corps was occupying Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this corps comprised three divisions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember the details.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Have you heard about the 12th Division of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And do you perhaps remember something about this 1st Corps, in other words, that it had 65.000 men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This comes to me as a surprise. I don't remember such figures.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at a map again, please. We still have the booklet on the ELMO. I would like the first map now to be shown to the witness. Could we magnify -- no, the other way around. Reduce it so that we could see -- can we see the entire map, please. Yes, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So a while ago we mentioned the yellow line, and you told me that the yellow line indicated the border between the -- or indicated where the Bosnian Army's positions were.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You don't remember, but we shall look at a number of other maps. I don't think this is a point that's challenged between the Prosecution and the Defence. This is the 12th Division of the 1st Corps which was inside this yellow line. Is that right? They had 75.000 men.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel Fortin has already responded at page 27, line 22, that he has never -- he doesn't recall if he heard about the 12th Division of the 1st Corps, so I hardly think he is in a position to answer a question formulated in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ask another question, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I shall put my question in another way.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether the -- a unit of the 1st Corps of the Bosnian Army was operating militarily within these yellow lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I can say is that some elements of the 1st Corps were inside the yellow lines, but the man we met in the presence of Mr. Gobilliard was a commander of the 1st Corps, General Ajnadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So my submission is now somewhat different. Inside the yellow lines, there was the 1st Corps, the entire 1st Corps of the Bosnian Army. Can we truly talk about a safe area when we talk about this area located inside the yellow lines? Let me remind you now of your statement. This is in paragraph 14(b), which we have mentioned already because one of your -- among your responsibility you needed to: [In English] "Maintain Sarajevo, Zepa, and Gorazde".

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: My submission, Your Honours, would be that this calls for speculation on the part of the witness, page 29, lines 5. Can we truly talk about the safe area when we talk about this area located inside the yellow lines? And indeed it's not a question he's in a position to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'd -- why not? He's a military man. I think he's in a position to answer it. I don't accept your submission.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, my submission would be the question as formulated is calling -- inviting speculation on the part of this witness. This Chamber is well aware, as are the parties here, that Sarajevo was, indeed, in 1993 declared a safe area by the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's not her question. You are to answer the question, Lieutenant, based on your experience.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you put your question again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I will not ask my whole question again, but what I said was: Can we say that Sarajevo was one of the safe areas so to speak insofar as within these yellow lines or inside these yellow lines there was an entire corps? You did identify this corps. You said that this corps was the 1st Corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why not? The United Nations declared these areas safe areas, and the blue helmets were mandated to maintain the confrontation lines and observe the confrontation lines. There were two warring parties, and the United Nations placed forces in these areas to make sure that the agreements are abided by, whether it would be agreement signed by two or three parties sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that according to the 4th Geneva Convention, I assume that the Canadian army is also concerned about the implementation of the -- these conventions provide for the area to be a safe area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: We do have the Geneva Conventions that provide for the fact that a particular region or territory could be called a safe area or be made or turned into a safe area. Do you agree with me that such convention on that -- that the Geneva Convention does exist and that all the armies in the world are preoccupied and concerned about the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I don't know all the articles of the -- of the said conventions admittedly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: That's not a problem because the Bench is familiar with the articles of the conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, if I understood you correctly, you were making a distinction between the formal declaration by the UN of a particular area as a safe area and whether, in fact, it was safe.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are absolutely right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And that is what I'd like the Lieutenant to answer because he must be in a position to answer that. Never mind the formal declaration as a safe area. On the basis of the experience that you had, was it a safe area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it was, and because it was declared so and because we were tasked to act in this light. The alternative was for all this area to become under Serb control, and this is what the UN wanted to prevent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You haven't answered the question, but proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another document before me in which we talk about a safe area. This document was admitted yesterday, it's document P21. Could you kindly display it. It's 65 ter 2479. That's the number. It's not a big problem. There was this document that was tendered yesterday. I thought I wrote down the right number. This is a document -- this is a memorandum written by Lieutenant-Colonel Fortin, signed by himself, dated June 28, 1995, meeting between General Smith and Colonel Meille on June 28, 1995. It is a 65 ter document. Maybe we can get some help. It's number 2479. So here the --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: P -- if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: -- P45 by my notes from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could have the second paragraph, please, where General Smith --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So these are questions we are going to deal with today are mentioned here. There's mention of the offensive and the attack against the television building by the Army of Republika Srpska, and he's wondering: [In English] Retaliation to the BiH attack or a simple violation of the safe area." [Interpretation] So here you were unable to answer to that question which is a question of fact. We wanted to know whether it was de facto a safe area, but you weren't able to answer so we'll continue anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, we will take the break now and may I ask how much longer you intend to be in your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need to compute how long it's already been. I think I've spent already 20 minutes, so I'll need about three times that, at least an hour and 15 minutes if possible. I believe that should be enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I believe you've spent more than 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Time flies. It's unfortunate technology is dragging us down a little.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I will discuss this matter with my colleagues, but I believe I'm going to have to set time-limits at the beginning of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In the circumstances, the Chamber will not give you another hour and 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have spent 45 minutes I've been informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And you will have another 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please continue, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let's move on to something else. Could we please display document 65 ter 471 -- 2471.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the document on your screen, Lieutenant-Colonel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know if it's the right one that I have on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This is a situation report, a weekly situation report, signed by David Harland.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could please have page 2, it's signed by David Harland. If we go to the paragraph saying: [In English] Last Friday and Saturday, Bosnian troops attacked Serb positions from the south-west and north." [Interpretation] So after this there's another paragraph starting: [In English] "By the end of the week it appeared that the Bosnians had made significant gains in only two areas: To the north of the city in the Cemerska heights and to the south of the city on the eastern slopes of Mount Igman." [Interpretation] So at the end -- almost at the end of this: [In English] "On Friday (23 June), the Serbs asked Civil Affairs to provide 500 body-bags, in expectation of upcoming casualties." [Interpretation] So does this document prove that there was a very intense Bosnian offensive going on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you -- were you an eye-witness to this -- to the intensity of the combat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was fully aware. I knew that Bosnians were trying to break the encirclement of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now have document 65 ter 2503.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This is another weekly situation report written by Mr. David Harland, and at page 2 you see right at the top of the page: [In English] "Two weeks after it began, the Bosnian offensive outside appears to have achieved very little." [Interpretation] Could you please confirm that this is almost at the end of June and that the offensive is still going on. Could you confirm that because I haven't heard you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please, could you look at this document on the screen, and I will read out: [In English] "On Wednesday" -- [Interpretation] This is the second paragraph. Do you have it? [In English] "Attack out of the city. The main attack came from the western part of the town and was focused on the Serb-held area of Nedzarici. The nearby areas of Stup and Rajlovac were also attacked." [Interpretation] Have you read this? Were you able to see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I can't see the paragraph. I can't seem to find it. I've found it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So what is written in this paragraph, is it exact? Is it correct? In your statement, if we could please have the paragraph 75 and 76 of the statement on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You're saying absolutely the same thing in your statement. [In English] "On June 28th the Bosnian army" -- [Interpretation] This is exactly the correct you made to your statement yesterday. [In English] "Started shelling Stup and Nedzarici." [Interpretation] You do remember this part of your statement, right? This is the passage that you corrected yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: If we could please now look at the map that is on the ELMO and try and locate Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the map on the screen, please, and if we could zoom in a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see Nedzarici and could you please point to Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now point to the PTT building where you were stationed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I think the two areas are close.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please also show us the TV building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's east of the PTT building.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: If we could now move to the other document that we've already seen, the 65 ter document 2503, and if we could move to page 3 of that document. So after the title -- can you read this? Can you read it on your screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It needs to be scrolled down a little bit. It needs to be scrolled down.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, scroll down. Right after the title that says: [In English] "Since the Bosnian offensive began two weeks ago, the number of Bosnian heavy weapons operating from near UNPROFOR facilities has significantly increased." [Interpretation] Could you please confirm this because in your statement also in paragraph 76 you mentioned this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. We're already somewhat familiar with this document, and I'd like to raise a point that was raised with respect to reference to this specific section of the document yesterday. Your Honours, this extrapolation from the document has failed to note that the paragraph dealing with the subject: "Location of Bosnian weapons a problem," in fact continues and concludes on the very next page and this, I would submit, Your Honour, is something that should be presented to the witness as a whole to put the comment in the proper context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If that is so, I entirely agree. Do you have that in your document, the continuation of the text?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we have the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but, Your Honour, I don't agree. But I want something else because I'm continuing with the statement, this witness's statement. This is what I'm working with and it confirms exactly the same thing. So maybe we could wait for that part of the statement which confirms and then you will see what my submission is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. I'd like to have the whole statement put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So now could I please draw your attention to paragraph 76 of your statement. [In English] "I was in the PTT building at the time this rocket fell on the TV building. It made a huge explosion. There were Bosnian mortars in the vicinity. They were in the field about 500 metres behind the TV building. The Bosnians put their mortars wherever they wanted, Kosevo hospital, the PTT building." [Interpretation] So do you think that we can reconcile what we saw in Mr. Harland's report, weekly report, where he states that the Bosnian Army is placing heavy weapons close to UNPROFOR positions. Is that exactly what you are saying in your declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I was saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe on the map, could you show us now these two locations. You were stationed in the PTT building --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: With respect, Your Honour, I don't think any reconciliation can be fairly made until the witness has the opportunity to see the whole paragraph in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's the paragraph to which you say continues?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: The specific paragraph that my learned friend is referring to, Your Honour, is the section -- deals -- it appears in the first instance at the bottom of page 3: "Location of Bosnian weapons a problem." That's the topic heading. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's the --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your indulgence for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Does it have a paragraph number?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, Mr. Harland's documents don't appear to have had paragraph numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on the third page after the subtitle --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: P19, Your Honour, is the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's on the third page, last subject heading: "Location of Bosnian weapons a problem." And Your Honours heard yesterday from Mr. Harland how the reports were structured. The -- if I could ask your indulgence, the next subject heading only appears later on on the following page. There's a concluding paragraph to that first subject heading, Your Honours, that I would submit is -- would be fairly put to the witness so he can contextualise his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So what is the -- it's the paragraph beginning --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Beginning on the next page, Your Honours. Continues the subject heading and reads: "Either way, there has been an increase in the number of Serb shells hitting UNPROFOR targets. The sector does not consider this to be wayward counter-battery fire from the Serbs but direct targeting."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And I will put it to the witness. This of course is something which could be done in re-examination, but I'll put it to the witness now.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And the question that is to be asked is whether in the light of that there can be a reconciliation. Colonel, the passage referred to by the Prosecutor reads: "Either way, there has been an increase in the number of Serb shells hitting UNPROFOR targets. The sector does not consider this to be wayward counter-battery from the Serbs, but direct targeting." In the light of that, what is the answer that you would give to the question that was asked by Ms. Isailovic earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I said, the Bosnians did set up some mortar positions near facilities such as PTT and TV building, but this was in course of their spring offensive to try and break out of Sarajevo and they were firing from many positions, usually mortars, for example, fire a few rounds from one position and then move to another one. So they did set up there, but I personally believe that the Serb retaliation which was usually quite accurate when it hit UN facilities it was direct targeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please tell us, Lieutenant-Colonel, one thing. In paragraph 76 of your statement, who -- who actually fired the rocket that fell on the TV building? Do you know who fired that rocket?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it came from Serb territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the question, you know, I want to ask is the following. Given the experience that you've had on the ground, was that because there were Bosnian weapons in the surroundings and that the Serbs were targeting those weapons, or do you think it was a deliberate attack on the TV building, which led to 32 wounded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to me, it was a deliberate shot. They were deliberately targeting that building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before continuing, can I ask a question on the time that is -- I have left. Could you please -- would that be ten minutes that all these comments took? I'm doing my best, you know, to really go through all the questions that I want to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Another 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I'll continue. I didn't want to know how you -- I'm not asking you how you evaluate all this now, but are these those heavy -- the same heavy weapons that you were mentioning in the paragraph 76 and that's your statement? Do you think it is the same heavy weapons that Mr. Harland is mentioning in his situation report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So on the map we saw that Nedzarici, maybe Rajlovac. Do you know Rajlovac? Do you know this place name? Does that ring a bell, Rajlovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is it close also to the PTT building and is it also close to the TV building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a few kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But at the time maybe you knew that these are very densely populated areas. These are urban areas, Nedzarici and Rajlovac are urban areas that are very densely populated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For Rajlovac, I can't really tell you whether it was densely populated, but Nedzarici, I don't think it was that densely populated when the combat occurred.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So you think that in Nedzarici there weren't that many civilians at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in the period of reference, you know, for around June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You think the people had left, is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Judge Mindua asked you a question which goes in the same direction as my question. You said that you thought this was a deliberate shelling, targeting the TV building, but as a military man, can you confirm to us that there were -- there were cross-fires and that the two warring parties were actually shooting at each other. I'm not talking about proportionality here, I'm just -- but was this exchange an exchange of fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there were exchanges of fire everywhere. There was fighting going on everywhere in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but at the time -- we're talking about at 8.30 in the morning when there was an attack on Nedzarici and Rajlovac, then at 9.00 there was the rocket that fell on the TV building. So militarily, could you talk about the firing that would be going on during combat, and we're not talking about intensity of fire or proportionality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can talk about exchange of fire but you cannot make a connection with a specific targeting of different areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You talked at length about another problem --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a second, Ms. Isailovic. Can you tell us why you say the TV building was specifically targeted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From -- Your Honour, from our estimate -- from what I recall, we had discussions about that at the headquarters Sector Sarajevo at the time. And we came to the conclusion that it was direct targeting, based on the fact that usually the Serb indirect fire was quite accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I have another question that springs to mind. You were talking about heavy weapons that were scattered everywhere throughout this limited area around the PTT building, and you're talking -- you say that there are mortars 500 metres behind the TV building. Could you please show us on the map exactly where those mortars were located. You have on the map the TV building and the PTT building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The TV building's right here and the field about 500 metres behind it, that's where there were mortars for a while.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But there's a little river here. On which side of the river were the mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the north side.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So you go behind the TV building, you cross the river. I know this, that Bojako Potok is there and this is a densely populated neighbourhood with houses.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, right at the north there's people and then it's sort of no population and that's where the mortars were.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: When you put heavy mortars here, in those places, does that change the civilian nature of an object when mortars are located close to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: There are military facilities and civilian facilities. A hospital, for example, is a civilian object in military terms, the PTT building also. But when close to it or inside possibly there are weapons in it. In such a facility, does this change the nature of the facility? Is the facility going to change in nature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think it can change the nature of object or places, but if you want to -- that's -- when you put your weapons there then, you know, you run into the problem of collateral damage of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to something else. We talked a lot about the hostage crisis between the Army of Republika Srpska and the UNPROFOR. You were closely involved in all -- in everything that happened there. Could you confirm to us that the hostage taking occurred after NATO bombed the territory that was held by Republika Srpska on May 25 and May 26, 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I remember right, yes, it was right after.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In a 65 ter document number 103, Mr. Harland on page 3 is mentioning the following: [In English] "-- NATO air-strikes last week" --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could we wait until we have the document on the screen, please, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. [Interpretation] On page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, this is what Mr. Harland says. Do we have the document on the screen? No. In your witness -- in your statement, you -- maybe you will remember. General Mladic said to General Janvier that a hostage taking was due to the NATO bombings and that the hostages would be released once the bombing stops. Do you remember this part of your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will have to look at it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: We have Mr. Harland's report here which mentions a hostage crisis which continues. You can see this, it's on the second sentence. So he establishes a connection between this hostage taking and qualifies it and says that this is a form of retaliation because of NATO bombing. Now, let's move on to paragraph 65. This is on page 12. Do you have this document in front of you? In paragraph 65: [In English] "General Smith told us that General Janvier had talked to General Mladic. Mladic purportedly said that the hostages were prisoners of war, and that he would not free any of them until he had a written guarantee from NATO that there would be no more air-strikes." [Interpretation] Can you confirm to me that you -- this is what Mr. -- what General Smith said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear this? Did you hear General Smith saying this, that General Janvier talked to General Mladic and that there was a connection between the hostage taking and the NATO bombing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this conversation being mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Was this punitive measure undertaken by the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps you should qualify this when you use the word "punitive." I think it was an attempt to implement the agreement which had been signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: We do have your statement. I'd like to turn to paragraph 33 now. For instance, you mentioned the ultimatums that had been drafted and that you drafted. This was part of your job. [In English] "For instance, around May 20, when the Bosnian Serbs started using weapons around the WCPs, we wrote letters. One that I wrote was an ultimatum that we gave them to return weapons to the WCPs, or that we would bomb. They did not and we bombed." [Interpretation] Can you confirm this? Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So it's important to record your answer in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 49 of your statement it says: [In English] "In response to the Bosnian attack, the Bosnian Serbs started to fire their weapons which had been gathered in the WCPs." [Interpretation] Can you confirm this now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I wrote.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: According to you, had NATO ever bombed the ABiH army units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And can we say that the violations committed by the Army of Republika Srpska, these violations were a form of retaliation against the attacks of the Bosnian Army that had used heavy weapons, and they used the heavy weapons which were being guarded by UNPROFOR. Was this the violation in question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you say that again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did the Army of Republika Srpska commit this violation? They had taken the heavy weapons which were under the protection of UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And in order to do so, they were punished and NATO decided to bomb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now turn to document 65 ter 2374 -- 2364.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This is also a weekly sit report dated the 19th of May and drafted by David Harland. This report was drafted before the bombing started because the NATO bombing started on the 25th and 26th of May. Is that right? And in this report it says --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't see the text yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This is on page 2. This is the paragraph which is just below: "Fighting around the city." [In English] "Both sides have begun using their heavy weapons with vigor." [Interpretation] And after it reads in the same paragraph at the end: [In English] "both sides used heavy weapons liberally, with the Serbs even firing from weapons nominally under the control of UNPROFOR in designated weapons collection points." [Interpretation] In the fifth paragraph [In English] "-- in the confrontation line." [Interpretation] Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to get back to the beginning of this page.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: The beginning of the page. This report was drafted before the bombing. This occurred before the events we are talking about, and Mr. Harland is talking about the fact that both parties were using heavy weapons. And I would like you to confirm that only one side was punished by NATO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to address - we don't have much time - one question that relates to the total exclusion zone and where no heavy weapons could be used. I would like to talk about Mount Igman, and in paragraph 14, again of your statement, it says about the responsibility and the way in which the Sarajevo Sector was organised. This is in paragraph 14(a), and you were, amongst other things, occupying the TEZ. Could you explain to us a little bit how this worked, how these exclusion zones worked, because I think you are an expert on this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think you would have to be more specific. I would like your question to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: What was the purpose of these zones? They were total exclusion zones in this sector. What does this mean? What were these total exclusion zones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Primarily, they were designed to protect the civilian population, to avoid fighting occurring in these zones, or preventing from munition to explode in these areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So the idea was to prevent fighting in these zones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and to make sure that heavy weaponry wasn't used.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, primarily heavy weaponry. So Mount Igman and the road to Mount Igman was also located in this zone. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And can you confirm this -- this goes beyond the time you were in Sarajevo, but from August 1993 these total exclusion zones had already been designated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, I don't know that period as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, this was before your arrival. Am I right in saying that the warring factions were not entitled to be there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This notion of total exclusion zones collapsed just before I arrived. I don't remember -- remember all of this so well because the whole thing collapsed soon after I arrived.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: A while ago we talked about safe areas and that collapsed also. So here we are dealing with another idea, and UNPROFOR was responsible for this and this was no longer working, but the idea behind this was that the warring factions were not allowed to go into these zones. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I was saying earlier on, it was to prevent fighting occurring in these zones; that was the primary objective, but I don't remember anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: However, but in your statement you recount what happened at the time. It seems that the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was present in these areas in mount -- close to Mount Igman and the road that led up to Mount Igman.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this zone was used by this army for military purposes; in other words, they were transporting arms and troops. Was that the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't confirm that because it's not something I saw personally. From what I could see and what was circulating was aid convoys that -- the UNHCR convoys that were trying to reach the town, the UNPROFOR convoys, but there were also civilian and Bosnian convoys that were trying to provide food to the town. I didn't see any military convoys or any Bosnian arms being transported.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, in paragraph 72 - I don't know if you have this front of you - [In English] "-- traffic jams" -- [Interpretation] And you say: [In English] "-- up and down at night at each end." [Interpretation] Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, they prevented UNPROFOR from using this area which had been allocated to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: UNPROFOR could have used one route and the airport also, but we were prevented from doing so by the Serbs. Yeah, in fact, there was Bosnian traffic on the Mount Igman road.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could go to the next page, please. In paragraph 78 you mention a man called Hajrulahovic. Could you tell us who this person is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember the name, but I can't remember what his position was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: What unit did he belong to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Bosnian military.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: On -- [In English] "-- I told him that movement of sector forces over Igman was acceptable, but movement of the -- [Interpretation] these rapid intervention forces that were not. Am I right in saying that Mr. Hajrulahovic is taking on more powers than he should have had in the area occupied by UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that's what he wanted --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's hear your objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: He's already said at page 51, lines 21 to 24 he can't remember the position of Mr. Hajrulahovic, so I hardly think the witness is in a position, not knowing Mr. Hajrulahovic's position, to comment on what powers he might have been able to have or to operate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Ask another question, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to shed light on this. The rank of Mr. Hajrulahovic is not something which is of interest to me. The witness answered by saying that he was Bosnian. I don't know. I could perhaps repeat my question. I'm just asking the witness to give me his view. Whatever his rank might have been in the army, I just wanted to say that this man was not part of UNPROFOR, but that he was occupying this area and he was amongst other areas occupying Mount Igman. And Mr. Hajrulahovic was actually in that area and giving instructions, whereas he shouldn't have been in that area in the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. All I can say, this is something I wrote in my statement. This Bosnian representative wanted to restrict the movements of the Rapid Reaction Force around Mount Igman but it was not possible. It was UNPROFOR and the Rapid Reaction Force that had the final or the last word.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So in that statement in paragraph 91, here you are -- 81. You're saying that there was a discussion between General Nicolai, he was Chief of Staff, it was Mr. Smith, General Smith's Chief of Staff and he had a conversation with Mr. Muratovic. So is he -- which side was Mr. Muratovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt again, but I see reference to the statement in paragraph 91 appearing in the transcript, and I note that paragraph 91 was redacted from this witness's statement. Are we referring to the proper paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 81, I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the witness got the right page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Reference is to 81.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So Mr. Muratovic, whose side is he on? He's on the Bosnian side, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he's a Bosnian -- he's a civilian, a Muslim civilian.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And so Mr. Nicolai?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicolai is a high-ranking official of UNPROFOR and he talked to this Mr. Muratovic, a civilian, a Bosnian civilian, and talking to him about how this zone which was supposed to be occupied by UNPROFOR is being used.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is that what this is all about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you please give me some time so I can read paragraph 81.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And you're very near to the end of your cross-examination now, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all I can say is the Bosnians expressed that desire. A bit further down I hint that things didn't turn out exactly the way they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But they did continue using Mount Igman and the Igman road. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Lieutenant-Colonel Fortin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Isailovic. Ms. Edgerton.
